title: Hierarchical Proxy Modeling for Improved HPO in Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Selecting hyperparameters is crucial for time series forecasting.

gap.claim: Classical temporal cross-validation for HPO can produce poor test performance because validation and test periods may mismatch.

contributions.claim: H-Pro drives HPO through test proxies by exploiting data hierarchies in time series datasets.
The method optimizes the lowest-level base forecaster using proxy forecasts for the test period generated by forecasters at higher levels.
H-Pro can perform HPO with any off-the-shelf machine learning model.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe H-Pro as a novel technique for addressing the test-validation mismatch.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive empirical evaluation on five publicly available hierarchical forecasting datasets.
The authors report that H-Pro outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on Tourism, Wiki, and Traffic datasets and achieves competitive results on Tourism-L without model-specific enhancements.
The authors report that H-Pro outperforms the winning method of the M5 forecast accuracy competition.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hyperparameter selection is important for time series forecasting.
Temporal cross-validation may mismatch validation and test periods, harming test performance.
H-Pro uses hierarchical test proxies and higher-level forecasts to optimize the lowest-level forecaster.
The approach is applicable to off-the-shelf machine learning models.
The authors evaluate H-Pro across five hierarchical datasets and report competitive or superior results on named benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the H-Pro algorithmic procedure in detail.
The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results or statistical significance.
The abstract does not identify the five datasets beyond the named Tourism, Wiki, Traffic, and Tourism-L datasets.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, sensitivity analyses, or reproducibility details.
